column1: # AMENDED 2026-10-25: THREE OF THE 659 IDS NO LONGER EXIST, so the row count
# is 656 live rows plus three that this inventory predates. Checked by
# intersecting every id in this file against the collector tree: 655 of 659
# resolve to a row whose current source still declares the size parameter named
# here, and the three that resolve to nothing are
# layers withdrawn from San Carlos's IDE - the evidence is in the group comment
# at the head of their old position in hp3b19_latam.c) and
# JO30_GOV_SETAGAYA_EXTINGUISHER (RENAMED, not removed: it is five district
# A fourth row's DATA is stale rather than its id: CR_SANCARLOS_PREDIOS is
# listed here as `maxfeatures`, and that row was re-pointed to WFS 2.0.0 on
# 2026-10-19 and carries `count`. It reads 20,000 a run over a cycle and is not
# Worth saying plainly because it cost something: two of those three phantom
# ids were carried out of this file into a session summary as live work to do,
# and the two rows had been retired with full evidence five days earlier. An
# inventory is dated the moment it is written; re-resolve its ids against the
# tree before treating any of them as a finding.
# CORRECTED 2026-10-25, BEFORE ANY FIX WAS BUILT ON IT. The header below is
# kept verbatim because its per-row data is sound and its conclusion is not:
# the 659 rows are real and almost all of them PAGE ALREADY. Read this block
# What the original pass measured: that each of these rows declares a page size
# whose spelling sits on jsonlist's EXTRA list rather than PAGERS. True.
# What it then CONCLUDED: that each therefore makes one request per run, and
# that two PAGERS entries would make all 659 walk. Both wrong, because the
# conclusion assumed every row reaches jsonlist_next_page(), and it never
# checked each row's own declared opts or its construct.
# Re-derived from the C, which is the maintained copy:
#          through declared opts and a PAGERS entry was never relevant to them.
#   300  VGEO rows (299 VGEO + 1 VGEO_IDKEYS). VGEO does not go through
#          lib/geojson.c has its own four-mechanism pager, and mechanism 1 is
#          precisely the ArcGIS case: on `exceededTransferLimit` it advances
#     2  VJSON rows -- the ONLY rows a PAGERS entry would have reached.
# So the proposed two-line engine change would have altered 2 rows, not 659.
# The cross-check that the new classification is the right one: it counts
# exactly 154 rows carrying `resultOffset`/`startIndex` in their own URL, the
# same 154 the column below reports, and attributes all of them to the hp half.
# THE REMAINING DEFECT IS SMALLER AND DIFFERENT. Of the 357 hp rows, 209 page
# with an order clause, 122 page by offset with NONE, 21 have no sortable field
# that could be established, and 5 declare no paging at all
# IE_EPA_AIR_SITES, IE_EPA_BATHING_WATERS -- all WFS rows on `maxFeatures`).
# AND THE 122 WERE MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, which is the only reason this
# file does not now recommend a 122-row edit as a recovery. One row per host,
# four requests each -- offset 0 and offset 50, unsorted, then the same two
# with `orderByFields=<the layer's own oid>` -- comparing OBJECT IDS, not
#   ALREADY_STABLE  15 hosts / 109 rows   unsorted overlap 0 of 50 on EVERY
#                                         host: they serve a stable order with
#   SHORT            3 hosts /  13 rows   the layer holds less than one page,
#                                         so there is no seam to lose
#   SORT_REFUSED     0                    the clause is accepted everywhere
#   SORT_IGNORED     0                    and honoured: sorted pages are
# So adding `orderByFields` to those 122 rows recovers NOTHING measurable
# today. It remains what CLAUDE.md's rule asks for -- an offset walk should
# name a stable sort -- and it is free, since every one of the 122 sits on a
# layer declaring `supportsOrderBy: yes`. But it is prophylaxis against the
# order changing, not a repair, and must not be reported as records recovered.
# ONE HONEST LIMIT ON THAT READING: those four requests completed in 10
# seconds. The 2026-10-24 SF 311 measurement showed a collision growing with
# walk DURATION (98 distinct of 100 in 26 s against 66 of 100 over 164 s),
# because an unordered index reshuffles under a slower walk. A 10-second probe
# is the fast case and cannot rule out loss on a walk that takes minutes.
# `orderByFields` CANNOT BE WRITTEN BLIND, which the layers themselves settled.
# 639 distinct layers were asked for their own metadata: 497 publish
# `objectIdField`, 109 more declare the id by TYPE (`esriFieldTypeOID`) while
# publishing no such key, and 33 were unreachable from here. Across them the
# id has TWELVE spellings -- OBJECTID 323, ObjectId 67, FID 49, objectid 35,
# ESRI_OID 7, OID 6, OBJECTID_1 4, fid 2, OBJECTID_12_13, OBJECTID_12,
# ObjectID, RowID. A batch writing `orderByFields=OBJECTID` would have been
# wrong on 35% of them, and a wrong field name is an ArcGIS error: it turns a
# row that reads one page into a row that reads nothing.
# THE TOOLING ATE THE DATA TWICE ON THE WAY TO THIS CORRECTION, and both are
# worth more than the finding. (1) The re-classifier blanked comments with
# `//[^\n]*`, which matched the `//` inside `https://` and blanked every URL in
# every file; the probe built on it reported "hosts: 0", which is the only
# reason it was caught. That is the FIFTH instance of that defect in this
# repo's tooling -- the fourth deleted 106,239 URLs and reported "0 pairs" as a
# RESULT -- and the resolver written the day before has the guarded
# `(?<!:)//`, so this was a regression introduced by retyping a pattern that
# already existed correctly. Its replacement is string-aware and asserts on
# every call that the count of `http` inside string literals is unchanged,
# refusing to return a tidy wrong answer. (2) The same script read each hp
# row's URL as the first `http` string in the row, which is `.portal` -- the
# human-facing site, not the request template -- so every hp row read as
# carrying no order clause. Both defects produced CLEAN-LOOKING output.
# WHAT WAS FIXED ON THE STRENGTH OF THE RE-DERIVATION, 2026-10-25. Eleven rows,
# 1,320,127 records that exist against 6,702 being read per run:
#     publishes `totalFeatures` in the same body, and geojson_emit_paged()'s
#     mechanism 3 advances a cursor when the total exceeds what was read AND
#     the URL already names one -- so the missing half was the cursor, not the
#     (startIndex 0 against 20, 20 + 20 features, overlap 0 on all eight).
#     Two of them declared maxFeatures=2000 and were served 1000 -- the
#     service's own cap, so every page came back short and a short page reads
#     as the end of the data; they declare 1000 now. Three BfS rows on the same
#     service are deliberately untouched because they are COMPLETE (8, 421 and
#     1,673 features). NOT exhaustive yet, and the file says so with the
#     arithmetic: the geojson ceiling is 20 pages, so a fixed row reads up to
#     20,000 a run, which completes only eurdep_latestValue (17 pages) and
#     discloses a shortfall up to 671 pages for gamma_aerosole. A VGEO row
#     cannot declare page_max/page_resume; the cycle needs these eight moved to
#     an hp table, where the ids and keys carry over unchanged.
#   2 VJSON rows, 1 record each of 6,072 and 29,208 -- and BOTH HAD A SECOND
#     DEFECT THAT MADE THE FIRST INVISIBLE: `array_path` was "fields", which in
#     an ArcGIS reply is the COLUMN DEFINITIONS, so each run emitted ~20 field
#     descriptors titled and keyed as remediation sites and zoning districts.
#     CLAUDE.md records that trap ("once counted a response's own 252-key
#     schema block as records") and these two rows shipped with it. Raising the
#     limit alone would have changed NOTHING while array_path named `fields`,
#     which is why the record count looked plausible. Now "features", with
#     `f=geojson` so each feature carries a top-level `id` for VJSON's key
#     precedence (an `f=json` feature is {attributes, geometry} with no scalar
#     at the top and would have keyed on a hash), `orderByFields` on the
#     layer's own id spelling, and the size at the layer's declared
#     maxRecordCount. Their stored uids are field names and are orphaned;
#     cleanup_stale_uids.py is the tool and has NOT been run, the live database
#     `array_path = "fields"` -- the same schema-as-records defect, in the only
#     `page_walk=1` row of the 659. NOT fixed here: origin/main carries a
#     different version of its file, so it waits for the rebase rather than
# Engine: the two PAGERS entries went in, with the EXTRA list removed as dead,
# and hpengine_test.c's 9i2 was REPOINTED rather than deleted -- it had used
# `maxFeatures=2` as its example of a size with no movable cursor, a class this
# change empties, so it now names an unrecognised spelling plus a declared
# total (the surviving path to that disclosure) and two new cases pin the
# ArcGIS and WFS families advancing. Gates after: build 0 warnings,
# hptest all rc=0, registry 57,527 unchanged with 0 never-runs.
# A page size the walk RECOGNISES and cannot ADVANCE - 659 rows, measured
# lib/jsonlist.c keeps two lists and they do different jobs.
#   PAGERS[]            size_param paired with a cursor_param.
#                       jsonlist_next_page() iterates THIS ONE, so a row whose
#                       page size is in it walks to the page ceiling.
#   jl_declared_size()  the same families PLUS an EXTRA list, today
# The EXTRA comment says exactly what being in it means: these are "the size
# spellings that have no cursor sibling this walk can move, because 'the page
# came back exactly full' is evidence of more data whether or not we know how
# So a scheduled VJSON row whose page size is spelled that way makes ONE
# request per run, forever, however large the layer, and discloses the full
# page as a truncation notice. The disclosure is honest - rule 2's half holds -
# and the data past page 1 has never been fetched.
# 659 scheduled rows are in that state: 635 ArcGIS REST on
# declared page sizes are mostly not small (315 rows at 1000, 175 at 500, 69 at
# 200, 54 at 2000), which is why nothing flagged them: a row reading 1,000
# features of a layer looks healthy from the record count alone, exactly as
# rule 4's "the numbers look fine" trap predicts.
# THE DETAIL THAT MAKES IT A DEFECT RATHER THAN A DESIGN CHOICE: 154 of the 659
# already carry `resultOffset` or `startIndex` in their own URL, and the walk
# still cannot use it, because the loop is over PAGERS size params and
# `resultRecordCount` is not one. The authors declared the cursor and the
# This is the `count`/`start` story one API family over. CLAUDE.md records it:
# 48 GOV.UK rows declaring page_walk AND page_resume read ONE page of three
# records a run until `count`/`start` was added to PAGERS, and the ceiling
# audit's "pages_read 1 against pages_needed 44,885" had been saying so the
# WHY audit_url_limits.py DOES NOT SEE THEM. Its default scope is
# only. `--generated` widens the paths, and its own docstring tells the reader
# to discount the result: "Treat even that as noise: the `vsrc*` fleet pages
# through jsonlist_emit_paged() at the macro level and the `hp*` tables page
# through declared opts ... so a generated row with `limit=60` is almost always
# being walked." That reasoning is TRUE for a size in PAGERS and FALSE for one
# in EXTRA, and the exception is 659 rows wide. The lesson is the narrower one:
# "the macro pages for it" is a claim about the PARAMETER, not about the macro.
# MEASURED LIVE, 2026-10-24, the way the `$limit`/`$offset` PAGERS entry was
# measured before it was added ("one URL per distinct host, 14 hosts ...
# returned different bodies on all 14"). One registered URL per host, forced to
# bodies compared and then the feature attributes compared:
#   DIFFERENT  47   disjoint features - the cursor is honoured, a PAGERS entry
#   OVERLAP     4   the cursor moved but the two pages SHARE features
#   SAME        4   the cursor is ignored; the walk would re-request page 1 and
#                   jsonlist's repeat-record guard would stop it. No loss, no
#                   gain: these hosts need their own answer
#   HTTP        5   refused or unreachable from here, including one service
#                   that answers 200 at offset=0 and 500 at offset=2
# THE FOUR OVERLAP HOSTS ARE THE REASON THE FIX IS NOT ONE LINE.
# services2.arcgis.com advance the offset and serve records the previous page
# already held - an index with no stable order, which is CLAUDE.md's worst
# shape: "a collision that is really a skip", where the visible half is a
# harmless duplicate and the invisible half is a record served to nobody.
# Measured, not inferred, which is the only reason it is known. So the repair
# is TWO parts and the second is not optional:
#   2. an ordering clause on every row that then starts paging -
#      `orderByFields=OBJECTID` for ArcGIS (or the layer's own id field),
#      `sortBy` for WFS - because an offset walk with no stable sort skips.
#      BC's GeoServer refuses `startIndex` without `sortBy` outright, which is
#      the better failure; ArcGIS does not refuse, it just quietly reorders.
# NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY. Adding those two entries changes the behaviour of 659
# rows at once, and part 2 is a per-row edit across 635 ArcGIS rows - batch
# scale, needing the gates and a re-measure. An ArcGIS layer honours
# (10.3+), so the 4 SAME hosts are expected and are not a bug to chase. The
# measurement is here so the work does not start from inference.
# Columns: `construct` is vjson or hp; `cursor_present` says whether the row's
# own URL already names the cursor the walk cannot move.
